bib.venue: AAAI-24 (Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence)

question: How can an LLM answer questions that need passages and structures from several documents without costly repeated prompting?
hypothesis: A KG over passages and document structures, traversed by a fine-tuned LLM agent, retrieves better context than flat or multi-hop retrievers.
contributions: Generally applicable KG construction (TF-IDF, KNN-ST, KNN-MDR, TAGME) over passages and structural nodes
KGP: LLM-based KG traversal agent for prompt context retrieval, fine-tuned to predict next supporting facts
Comparison of traversal agents and KG densities, case studies

method.summary: Builds a graph over passages (edges by shared keywords, embedding KNN, or shared Wikipedia entities) plus page and table nodes. A fine-tuned T5 (or LLaMA) agent generates the next evidence passage and picks the neighbour most similar to it, expanding from TF-IDF seed passages up to a budget K; retrieved passages go to an LLM reader.

other.structural_questions: LLM classifies question as structure or content; structure keywords map to page/table nodes; table node returns markdown, page node returns one-hop passages

limits: Sample sizes, hyperparameters, prompts and metric definitions are in a separate Supplementary not in the PDF
No seeds or significance tests stated
KGP-T5 is not best on every cell (MDR wins IIRC, TF-IDF edges HotpotQA Acc) despite the text
Authors hypothesise, without testing, that LLaMA-7B needs more fine-tuning data than T5-0.7B
Denser KGs raise latency; KG density and construction are dataset-tuned (MDR encoder trained on HotpotQA)
Graph nodes are passages, not entities or relations: no typed relations or Cypher-style queries
